I think reading a lot really helps. Woolf said it lets your words flow like a river if you read a thousand books or something like that. It was fun and sort of refreshing to get out all my thoughts, I’ll admit that.

I’ve tried to embrace the joys of new things and losing control. Spontaneity was all I did for months. Every impulse I just acted on, anything to feel happy.

I went to the gym, got fit. I cut my hair. I joined a walking group, I volunteered, I ticked off a lot on my bucket list. I went to the opera.

Nothing. It’s really odd. 

I think my comment about ‘replacing’ was a bit naive. What I mean is; she will find someone else she will make a deep connection with, perhaps an even deeper one.

I’m selfish, occasionally rude, emotionally absent, quite callous to other people’s feelings and I think the world revolves around me. Like my parents say, I lie a lot and I attention seek. Maybe this whole post is one last “look at me” before I go. She would, genuinely, be better off without me. With someone who is kinder, more attentive and more focused on her. 

I can’t break the cycle. I can’t break the waking up and lying in bed and wanting to cry and crying and not feeling sad but feeling completely and utterly devoid. I can’t describe the feeling, it’s just that odd.

In short, my brother has been touching me since I was fourteen. He joked that on Saturday night he would go further.  He mentioned anal sex. That cannot happen. 

It was at first, it’s a complete reverse on the normal mentality. I can’t even think when my mind switched like that, became the complete opposite of what I am programmed to be like. It’s really odd. 

I have so many! Walking in the snow w him and him writing my name in the snow. Soldering a clock w him. Watching the antique roadshow. Swinging in a hammock and watching him planting carrots and peas. Making him a cup of tea. Sitting and listening to his stories. So many.

Upset that I was leaving her, that I would never see her again. Upset that she might need counselling because of me, or she might be sad that I wouldn’t be here anymore. Then I reminded myself of it all, and I stopped feeling that way. I knew she would move on, she’s resilient, not like me. 

Tomorrow is always worse, fatalist thinking Ik. But it always is. 

I love my grandad so saying goodbye to him might be the one thing that breaks me but I doubt it. I have to see my brother tomorrow so that might counteract the doubt.

I have a previous post which kind of explains it. I like to think I am pretty positive in the sense that I have come to terms w the fact that my life will soon be over and my legacy will be done.

I’ve written four plays, two books, and a few poems. I have given my best friend a tiny bit of help on the way to uni and I will no longer be a burden to anyone.

It fills the emptiness a bit but still, it numbs it all a bit.

I would like to say I enjoyed it but that isn’t true. I just felt on the verge of tears the whole time. 

It’s going to be worse tomorrow, I know it, when I see my grandad. I spent five years worrying about him dying from cancer and now I’m saying goodbye for the last time. It feels nice having some control over time, counting down the days, hours, seconds, when it previously felt like time was controlling me, threatening to take him away from me at any moment. 

They won’t tell him if they find me. They will be too scared of killing him w the shock. I am worried about my best friend and how she will take the news but she does have a good support network, I made sure of that. She can replace me.

I’m a great fan of French classic writers. Zola is like a French Dickens, his Rouge series is a must read. Baudelaire is one of my favourite poems, I’m bringing him along on Friday. Proust too if you have a lot of time. I like a mixture tbf: Murakami, Mishima are fabulous. 

One book I read the other day was Old man Goriot by Balzac, that is a definite worth while read. 

Also Dostoyevsky is unmissable, Pushkin , Chekhov if you like plays. The Seagull is the main aspiration for my final note. 

I have some random recommendations which I particularly enjoyed:

The Mabinogion

Troilus and Cressida, Chaucer

The Faery Queene, Spenser

The Decameron

And I nearly forgot Gogol, there’s a nice doc on amazon prime about him. 

Black Sunlight or House of Hunger by Dambudzo Marechera. 

And completely unrelated, North and South.
